The Audit Coordinator will oversee responses to audits of grants and contracts awarded to [Company name masked] by Federal and Non-Federal sources.
This position will lead entrance exam conferences, collaborate with campus representatives to fulfill audit requests, interpret and explain complex information, respond to potential findings, interact directly with project sponsors and subrecipients related to financial reporting, invoicing, payments, and auditing on behalf of the university to ensure compliance.
cond_0633.responsibilities:
Oversees and carries out compliance activities related to research at a program, department, divisional, or institutional level. Develops and executes the implementation of operations to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.
15% Develops, implements, and evaluates policies and procedures related to compliance with federal, state, local, and/or university regulations
15% Assists principal investigators, researchers, administrative staff, leadership, and others to ensure institutional compliance with applicable regulations
40% Ensures institutional compliance related, but not limited to: audit coordination, conflict of interest, intellectual property, and institutional review boards, export controls, effort, or other policies
15% Serves as a key resource to campus regarding research administration compliance areas and may supervise staff
10% Complete central subrecipient risk assessments and communicate any adjustments to subrecipient monitoring to RSP accountants and department staff
5% Manage a small portfolio of NSF awards and help other RSP accountants with their portfolio duties
cond_0633.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related business field, or equivalent practical experience.
Around 5 years of experience in business, accounting, or financial management, including some grant and contract experience.
Ability to analyze, interpret, and apply Federal, State, and University policies and procedures.
Ability to analyze and interpret university accounting systems and data.
Willingness to build working relationships across a diverse workforce at all levels.
Preferred Requirements
Audit experience is a plus.
Comfort communicating complex situations and ideas through written and oral formats.
Experience working collaboratively with a range of stakeholders.
Familiarity with changing technologies that affect business processes.
Background in communication, planning, problem-solving, organizational, project management, and customer service.
We evaluate candidates holistically and consider relevant education, training, and transferable experience.

15% Develops, implements, and evaluates policies and procedures related to compliance with federal, state, local, and/or university regulations
15% Guides principal investigators, researchers, administrative staff, leadership, and others to ensure institutional compliance with applicable regulations
40% Ensures institutional compliance related, but not limited to: audit coordination, conflict of interest, intellectual property, and institutional review boards, export controls, effort, or other policies
15% Serves as a key resource to campus regarding research administration compliance areas and may supervise staff
10% Leads central subrecipient risk assessments and determines any adjustments to subrecipient monitoring, communicating outcomes to RSP accountants and department staff
5% Manages a small portfolio of NSF awards and supports other RSP accountants with their portfolio duties
cond_0647.requirements:
Bachelor's Degree
Degree in Accounting, Finance, or other business related degree is preferred.
Five (5) years of business, accounting or financial management experience preferred, which includes grant and contract experience. Audit experience strongly preferred.
Ability to analyze, interpret and implement Federal, State, and University policies and procedures.
Ability to analyze and interpret University accounting systems operations and data.
Excellent communication, planning, problem-solving, organizational, project management and customer service skills.
Ability to clearly communicate complex situations and ideas through written communication and oral presentation.
Ability to influence and build working relationships among a diverse workforce at all levels.
Possess a proven ability to work collaboratively with stakeholders.
Possess an aptitude and curiosity toward changing technologies that impact business processes.

cond_0648.intro:
[Company name masked]'s Office of Research and Sponsored Programs (RSP) handles administration of extramural research grants and contracts. RSP currently manages an open portfolio of over $4 Billion with annual awards over $1 Billion. The Audit Coordinator will work with campus representatives and project sponsors to coordinate responses to audits of grants and contracts awarded by Federal and Non-Federal sources.
This position will help facilitate entrance conferences, work alongside campus representatives to fulfill audit requests, interpret and explain complex information, respond to potential findings, and coordinate directly with project sponsors and subrecipients on financial reporting, invoicing, payments, and auditing on behalf of the university to help ensure compliance.
